48	#include <cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp>
49	namespace sg { namespace sm90 { namespace cute_gemm {
50	struct TmaPlan { CUtensorMap desc; /*128B POD*/ };

61	  CUtensorMap`). It is a 128-byte POD; memcpy the descriptors into a device buffer
62	  (`cudaMalloc` + `cudaMemcpy`) so the kernel reads them from global. (Alternatively

106	### 2.1 Static layout objects (compile-time, zero register cost)
107	```cpp

109	using Atom = SM90::GMMA::MMA_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS;   // N=128 default

134	   fence helper — it is the same `wgmma.fence.sync.aligned` PTX), then

136	   GMMA::ScaleOut::One))`. CuTe's atom `fma` emits the identical `wgmma.mma_async`

141	   independent fragments sharing one B descriptor (mirrors issue_k,
142	   model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:750-762). CuTe fragment = `Atom`'s C-fragment type

171	  `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor ≥ 1` cert (:1540-1545) is the

175	- **GridBarrier:** untouched. The CuTe GEMM runs ENTIRELY between `ctx.barrier()`
176	  calls (megakernel fwd/bwd/dW phases). TMA's mbarrier is a CTA-LOCAL smem barrier
177	  (different mechanism from the cross-CTA `GridBarrier`); they do not interact. No
178	  cluster ⇒ no `ClusterBarrier`, no cooperative launch — the hand `GridBarrier`

182	  issue order (same invariant the cp.async ring + PIPE=2 engine preserve,

207	  - `test_decoder_tc.py::test_fwd_random` (rel≤2e-2 vs fp64), `test_fwd_identity`.
208	  - **Crucially `test_determinism_bitwise`** and the full-cell

210	    rel ≤ 1e-4. This proves the CuTe MMA atom is bit-equivalent to the hand wgmma.
211

148	
149	1. **TMA inside a persistent, non-cluster kernel.** The `cp.async.bulk.tensor`
150	   PTX is `shared::cluster`-scoped but valid at cluster-size-1; the only
151	   requirement is a properly-init'd mbarrier + `expect_tx`. The existing
152	   `Mbarrier` (warp_specialize.cuh) already issues exactly the right PTX. The TMA
153	   descriptor is a 128 B `CUtensorMap` that MUST be created HOST-side (the
154	   `cuTensorMapEncode*` driver call is host-only) and live in `__grid_constant__`
155	   or global memory; we pass a device pointer to it via `PersistentContext`. One
156	   descriptor per (operand-tensor, layout) — for the decoder that is per-weight-
157	   matrix + per-acts-region (≈ a few dozen). A `prefetch.tensormap` / fence is
158	   needed if the descriptor is read from global the first time (cheap, once).
159	2. **Occupancy / register pressure vs 1-CTA/SM.** The GMMA atom's accumulator is
160	   `N/2` fp32 regs/thread (64 for N=128) — identical to today's `WgmmaAccum`, so
161	   no NEW register cost from the MMA. The risk is CuTe's `Tensor`/`Layout` algebra
162	   bloating the addressing (the hand path is hand-minimal). Mitigation: use the
163	   atom's `fma(desc_a, desc_b, frag_c)` directly with hand-built descriptors (CuTe
164	   `make_gmma_desc` is `constexpr`/cheap), NOT a full `TiledMMA::partition` dance
165	   per k-step. The launcher's `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocks≥1` cert (megakernel
166	   :1540) is the existing safety net — if CuTe regalloc drops occupancy below 1
167	   CTA/SM the launch REFUSES (no hang), and the SG_TUNED flag stays OFF.

169	   2-SM/threadblock-cluster + many CTAs co-scheduling tiles. We keep the project's
170	   OWN tiling (kTileM=128, kIL=2, token-tile-parallel) and only swap the per-tile
171	   inner GEMM transport+MMA to CuTe atoms. The grid scheduler stays the hand-built

176	## D. DETERMINISM PRESERVATION (the A/A/A + fp64 gate)
177	
178	The CuTe path MUST reproduce the EXACT fp32 reduction order. This holds **by
179	construction** if:
180	- The MMA atom is the SAME `m64nNk16 f32.bf16.bf16` op (CuTe's
181	  `MMA_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS::fma` emits the identical `wgmma.mma_async` PTX as
182	  the hand `wgmma_issue_n128`). Same hardware op ⇒ same intra-tile reduction.
183	- The k-loop is the SAME ascending order, k=0 ScaleD=0 (overwrite) / k>0 ScaleD=1
184	  (accumulate). CuTe's atom `fma` takes a `scale_D`/`accumulate` arg — drive it the
185	  same way (first issue accumulate=false). TMA changes only WHEN a tile lands, not
186	  the issue order (same property the existing cp.async ring + PIPE=2 engine already
187	  preserve, model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:876-886).
188	- The smem operand BYTES are bit-identical: TMA into a `Layout_K_INTER_Atom`
189	  (no-swizzle) tile reproduces the hand `idx(mn,k)=(k/8)*(MN*8)+mn*8+(k%8)` layout
190	  EXACTLY, so the GMMA descriptor reads the same core matrices. (If we adopt
191	  128B-swizzle, the smem bytes differ but the MATH the wgmma computes is identical
192	  — the descriptor + TMA agree on the swizzle — and fp32 accumulation order is
193	  unchanged. Still, START with no-swizzle = byte-identical smem to de-risk.)
194	- The epilogue fragment decode is the SAME. CuTe's `partition_fragment_C` gives the
195	  same thread→(row,col) map as `wgmma_frag_decode` (both implement PTX §<ip>.3);
196	  but to be SAFE and to keep ONE source of truth, reuse `wgs::wgmma_frag_decode` in
197	  the epilogue (the gate already validates it).
198	- No float atomics; one CTA owns the tile end-to-end (unchanged — the scheduler is
199	  untouched). The dW split-K reduce stays the deterministic ascending-chunk reduce
200	  (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:96-101).
201

254	### 6b. THE TMA BLOCKER (critical) — CUtensorMap is HOST-only in CuTe v3.6.0
255	- The ONLY descriptor-creation path in CuTe v3.6.0 is `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, called
256	  from `make_tma_copy` which is a HOST driver call (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1008,1268).
257	  CuTe v3.6.0 has NO device-side tensormap encode (no `tma_descriptor_replace` /
258	  device `cp_async_bulk_tensor` map-build helper found in copy_sm90_tma.hpp).
259	- IMPLICATION: a TMA `SM90_TMA_LOAD` needs a `CUtensorMap` built ON THE HOST and passed
260	  into the kernel as a `const __grid_constant__ CUtensorMap` arg. The persistent
261	  megakernel takes its tensors as raw `float*`/`DecoderTokenCtx` (fused_decoder_
262	  megakernel.cuh:674-678) and the operands (acts buffer, C1/C1-T weight cache) are
263	  CARVED FROM THE WORKSPACE AT RUNTIME (dec_acts_bind / dec_wbf_bind,
264	  model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:419-438,506-524) — their addresses are not known host-side
265	  at launch in a fixed way per GEMM. So a full TMA path requires EITHER (i) building the
266	  tensor maps host-side once per step (the acts/weight-cache base ptrs ARE stable within
267	  a step → feasible: pass an array of `CUtensorMap` for the ~8 weight matrices + acts
268	  regions as grid-constant args), OR (ii) keeping cp.async staging and using CuTe ONLY

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

594	//  K-chain mainloop helper — the choreography in one call (the integration
595	//  seam the model headers invoke for a K-tile chain). DESIGN §3.1.
596	//
597	//  Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues over a fixed ASCENDING k-order (the
598	//  determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, k ascending, no
599	//  work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise-reproducible). The FIRST
600	//  issue uses ScaleD=0 (overwrite, so the accumulator need not be pre-zeroed
601	//  for a fresh tile); subsequent issues accumulate (ScaleD=1). One
602	//  wgmma_fence() before the group, one commit_group()+wait_group<0>() after.
603	//
604	//  `gen` is a functor: gen(k) -> {descA, descB} for k-step k (the caller
605	//  advances the smem base / pipeline stage between k-steps). Keeping the
606	//  descriptor generation a callback is what lets the SAME mainloop serve the
607	//  unpipelined gate (gen reads a fixed pre-staged tile array) and the
608	//  pipelined gate (gen reads the current ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical
